pr_body:
Closes #4829, closes #4344

Add a new 'Interrupted' field to `IBasicResult`. This is set to true if the operation was interrupted (e.g. by `run-script-before`).
Interrupted and failed backups are recorded in the job log (#4829).
When the backup is interrupted or fails (`Interrupted==true` or `ParsedResult=Fatal`), metadata for the server database is not updated (#4344).

If exceptions are caught from an operation this previously resulted in an error message in the server log. Now the error message is also recorded in the job log. ~~This has to create a new Operation in the database for now, so the logs are not linked to the performed changes in the database yet.~~

There are two new translation needed (to display "Fatal error" or "Interrupted" in the job log). I put these messages above the time, please suggest other options:
![screenshot of log entry with fatal error](https://github.com/duplicati/duplicati/assets/33495614/f3f141df-5aec-475d-9e3b-0cb1912b8e67)

Also, maybe a darker shade of red and a different icon could be used for the icons of fatal errors, so they can be spotted easier. I don't have the tools installed to change the stylesheet.

Thanks for taking the time to fix #4829 😃

> I put these messages above the time, please suggest other options:

I would like to suggest different formatting, but first would like to discuss the various operation result status types:

If I understand correctly, you are referring to 4 types (success, warning, error, fatal error) - and thus also suggest a darker red hue for fatal errors.

What is the difference between an error and a fatal error?

Due to #4829, I only operations with either 0 warnings and errors or operations with warnings only, listed on the job specific log page. So suggesting any job with at least one error is equivalent to a fatal error (operation was not completed)

I would like to suggest we use 3 result types (at least when displaying to the user):
- green/success: operation completed with no warnings
- yellow/warnings: operation completed, but encountered at least one warning
- red/failure: operation not completed, due to encountering at least one error

This is aligned e.g. with compiler warning/error classification (where warning means the operation can continue, whereas error means the operation will fail).

I'm not familiar enough with Duplicati's codebase, suggesting sticking to 3 types of operation completion status from a user perspective.

Am I missing anything?

> What is the difference between an error and a fatal error?

From a programming perspective (as implemented now):
A fatal error throws an exception that escapes the function that is supposed to run the operation. For a normal error, the operation returns normally, but there are error messages in the result log.

From a user perspective, maybe there are errors with only limited impact, so some of the backup still worked?

The fatal result code already existed, it was just never used. It is also useful to know that this run probably has no valid metadata (backup size etc.). We can of course display it the same as normal errors in the UI.

> Due to #4829, I only operations with either 0 warnings and errors or operations with warnings only, listed on the job specific log page. So suggesting any job with at least one error is equivalent to a fatal error (operation was not completed)

I don't think this is true. If you can produce an error that only writes an error message and does not throw an exception, or the exception is caught internally, you should get a result with errors in the job log. I think I had one of those for testing, but I would have to find it again.

## Edit
Non-fatal errors I could find:
- BackendQuotaExceeded in backup
- In database recreate, any error is treated as non-fatal and it is tried to continue
- RemoteFileVerificationError, FailedNewIndexFile, FailedExtraFileCleanup, FileAccessError, RemoteFileAccessError, CleanupMissingFileError in repair
- PatchingFailed, RestoreFileFailed in restore
- RemoteFileProcessingFailed, FailedToProcessFile in test

It is also possible to make other errors non-fatal by catching their exceptions, as long as it is reasonable to continue after them.
Got it. In this case, I propose the following:

![image](https://github.com/duplicati/duplicati/assets/77799839/c46ad452-eebc-488d-aa5b-2e732cb963b0)

When expanded, each result contains the list of fatal errors (if any), errors, and warnings.

The header row of each result (i.e. what's seen both when the result is collapsed and when it is expanded) reflects the most severe status:
- Fatal error: Date, time - Operation: Blah failed
- Error: Date, time - Operation: Blah (x errors)    [no matter how many warnings, only errors show at the collapsed state]
- Warning: Date, time - Operation: Blah (y warnings)
- Success: Date, time - Operation: Blah

Proposed styling for the new "Fatal" state (ResultIcon):
`"fa fa-stop-circle fatal-color"`

Adding the following to base.less:
```
.fatal-color {
    color: #990000;
}
```

**Note:** I only have very partial understanding of your code change, but it seems to me the content of the fatal error itself (i.e. the message of the exception that caused the fatal error) might not currently be propagated and saved?
(the content that would appear once "Fatal errors" is expanded in my mock screenshot)
@taz-il I like the design. There was also #4838 that integrates some stats. I guess those would only show for success then?
Do you think the square stop icon would be confused with a manually stopped job?

> Note: I only have very partial understanding of your code change, but it seems to me the content of the fatal error itself (i.e. the message of the exception that caused the fatal error) might not currently be propagated and saved?
(the content that would appear once "Fatal errors" is expanded in my mock screenshot)

Yes, right now it is written to the other error messages. I am not sure how the fatal error message could be distinguished from a normal error. There are separate fields for messages, warnings and errors in the result object, but not for fatal errors. Also the logger does not have a fatal category.

I could maybe add a single string for fatal error message (I don't think there could be two), but the whole result code is pretty tangled, with nested results which all need to be propagated.

Another compromise would be to replace the error section with fatal errors and assume that all of the error messages are relevant.
@taz-il do you have an idea where to put the message for interrupted backups? Maybe it would be enough in the title line, or it could replace the right side (Source files), because those statistics would be collected after and are always zero.

I would also like to discuss how to call the "Interrupted" result. This currently appears when the script indicates that the backup should not run (with an exit code). Since that is *before* the actual job starts, maybe it should better be called "Skipped"? I also thought about "Aborted", but that has a connotation of an error which is not always the case. 

I decided to hide the source file statistics for interrupted backups and leave the fatal errors only for the header for now:
![screenshot updated graphics](https://github.com/duplicati/duplicati/assets/33495614/c129d316-280d-4c9a-b80e-c82615ea5a23)
Hello

Thanks, very interesting change.

A few observations: it's logical indeed to hide stats when the job has been interrupted; however when the job has failed from a fatal error, the stats are wrong too and should be hidden IMO. See below

Also I have tried to find another icon because the one you picked is difficult to make apart of the one for error, warning..., while this case is different. What do you think of this one ? (also advice wanted from @ts678, @taz-il ; if you want to search for a better one, the source is here: https://fontawesome.com/v4/icons/ - we can't use v5 and the brand icons are verboten. I have also considered the flash, the broken link; no icon has made me think 'ahah this is the one !')

![image](https://github.com/duplicati/duplicati/assets/44170243/113dbb04-ff75-4f67-b981-c177fa2bcc27)

As you can see I have also mixed #4976 to test. 

BTW I have used the procedure by @ts678 in https://github.com/duplicati/duplicati/issues/4129#issuecomment-599149786 to test this change, because I still want to commit #4967 and add an error message hinting to check the backend, something along the lines of 'if failed or interrupted log error message "consider to test your backend"', and I think this PR is the best place to add it (if you don't want to I can add a separate PR of course once this one has landed)

> What do you think of this one ?

I guess that's "fire" on their page. I suppose that idea fits some cases. Are there any where this would come up upon request?

A more neutral approach to operations that just don't finish is to use minus-circle (to keep the circle theme) or minus-square. Minus suggests something is missing (specifically, completion is missing, right?). times-rectangle might work for an emphatic version of the current error which I think uses times-circle. I'm not sure I like tweaking the shade of red a little to make a fatal.
An icon that would be noticably different and still fit with the circle would be "ban" 🚫, but the meaning is slightly off. "fire" works for the meaning, but I couldn't identify the icon on first glance and the shape doesn't fit the others.

> it's logical indeed to hide stats when the job has been interrupted; however when the job has failed from a fatal error, the stats are wrong too and should be hidden IMO.

I agree they are most likely wrong, but depending on when the failure occurred the stats might be helpful for debugging. So I'm not sure if we should hide them completely.

> something along the lines of 'if failed or interrupted log error message "consider to test your backend"',

That is a good idea, but I would only do it for failed, since interrupted is intended behavior and shouldn't break anything. I think you should be able to commit on this branch directly, if not just tell me the changes.
> An icon that would be noticably different and still fit with the circle

I don't think it absolutely must fit with the circle, which is why one of my thoughts was a square which is noticeably different.
Regarding meaning, I proposed a minus (which seems to fit better than the reverse-slash inside a ban circle), but x might do, provided (ideally) something else changes to make it distinctive. Two other ways to indicate something was incomplete may include not shading in the circle (sort of like "ban" above), but are those harder to see? Maybe they stand out as "different"? "times-circle-o" would qualify, if you buy that argument. It uses usual error "x" but indicates it didn't finish, by being unfilled.

At the risk of complicating things, I think the tray icon is a Duplicati icon, and I don't think it distinguishes fatal from an error. Someone could look at the code. Maybe it's only red on a fatal error because there was also an error logged and recognized.

[Feature request: Additional tray icon status styles #3861](https://github.com/duplicati/duplicati/issues/3861) and associated PRs show some history about the visual tweaks there.

Following that thought into the total experience, I got an email about a failed backup (another Backblaze 503 with no retries). Looking closer, the status bar said `Error!` while my slow script after backup ran, and the tray icon was green while script ran.
Amusing temporary lack of coordination on the different signaling, but not a huge deal IMO, and eventually I got a lot of red.
EDIT: but not everywhere. Tray icon goes red, and GUI has a red error popup saying "One or more errors occurred." and `Show` button which takes me to the job log where there's nothing, but I guess that's the problem that these changes intend to fix...

I have `send-mail-level` set to `Warning,Error,Fatal`, but I now have a better idea of the difference between last two. Thanks!

----------------------------------------

## Environment info
<!-- Please include some relevant information about your environment. -->
<!-- For "Backend", please indicate the backup destination (e.g. Amazon S3, OneDrive, FTP, WebDAV, local). -->
- **Duplicati version**: 2.0.6.3_beta_2021-06-17
- **Operating system**: Win 11 Pro, 22H2
- **Backend**: FTP

## Description
<!-- Describe the issue that you are experiencing below. -->
When a backup job fails, the failures only appear on the general server page (the one for all backups), and not on the log page of the individual backup job that failed. As an example, I have this job running daily. It failed consecutively on Oct 1, 2, 3, etc, but these failures don't show up (is it only for me? is this the intended behavior for some reason?)

## Steps to reproduce
This happens with every backup failure, so in order to reproduce, just cause a backup to fail (e.g. wrong user/pass for FTP; or any other way).

<!-- For "Actual result", describe what happens after you run the steps above (i.e. buggy behavior). -->
<!-- For "Expected result", describe what should happen after you run the steps above (i.e. corrected behavior). -->
- **Actual result**:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/77799839/196005616-4ea8a06a-f3c6-4b72-8e63-6056fab15d94.png)
- **Expected result**:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/77799839/196005716-e7fb13e6-7753-4957-91d7-60e222426fe6.png)

Expected: all backup attempts show up in the log (not only the successful ones), with a minimum of "Backup failed" title, ideally with some short description of the error (e.g. "host unreachable"), but this latter part is of course lower prio.

This sounds like [Combine logs in GUI #1152](https://github.com/duplicati/duplicati/issues/1152). Sounds undesired and unintended but due to unstated technical reasons.
My usual guess (not confirmed by anybody knowing code well) is that the job logs (see `Complete log`) are results like:

https://github.com/duplicati/duplicati/blob/666b2281032460254839fdc3b6e1055fdf7ce1db/Duplicati/Library/Interface/ResultInterfaces.cs#L122

https://github.com/duplicati/duplicati/blob/666b2281032460254839fdc3b6e1055fdf7ce1db/Duplicati/Library/Interface/ResultInterfaces.cs#L32

The database LogData table looks like a backup actually writes the results when it has them -- unless it errors out early.

https://github.com/duplicati/duplicati/blob/666b2281032460254839fdc3b6e1055fdf7ce1db/Duplicati/Library/Main/Operation/BackupHandler.cs#L572

https://github.com/duplicati/duplicati/blob/666b2281032460254839fdc3b6e1055fdf7ce1db/Duplicati/Library/Main/Database/LocalDatabase.cs#L1434

https://github.com/duplicati/duplicati/blob/666b2281032460254839fdc3b6e1055fdf7ce1db/Duplicati/Library/Main/Database/LocalDatabase.cs#L358

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/40771998/197368137-4f6c0d0a-7423-4dc3-b214-9bb23eb892d4.png)

Even though the log is structured data, I don't know why there couldn't be a version with a little error info and no more.
Possibly it has to do with how the exceptions flow. If anyone does C# and would like to look, take the above as starters...
I would definitely love to see this improved, but somebody needs to volunteer, and volunteers are extremely scarce now.
